questions.question: Which attribute on an <iframe> is mandatory for accessibility so screen readers understand its content?
questions.hint: A human-readable title describing the frame.
questions.explanation: WCAG requires a descriptive 'title' attribute on every <iframe> so screen reader users know what content is embedded.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the sandbox attribute on an <iframe>?
options: It scales the iframe down to mobile proportions
It applies security restrictions, disabling scripts and forms unless explicitly permitted
It accelerates frame rates using WebGL
It converts HTTP connections to HTTPS
questions.explanation: The sandbox attribute restricts scripts, popups, and origin access to prevent malicious code from compromising the host page.

questions.question: Which attribute value allows a sandboxed iframe to execute JavaScript code?
questions.explanation: allow-scripts allows the sandboxed frame to run its own JavaScript scripts.

questions.question: How can you prevent an offscreen iframe from consuming bandwidth before the user scrolls to it?
questions.explanation: loading="lazy" instructs the browser to defer loading the iframe until it nears the user's viewport.

questions.question: Which HTTP response header sent by a server prevents external websites from embedding its pages in an <iframe>?
questions.explanation: The X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors) header prevents the page from being rendered inside an iframe anywhere.
